title: VideoDerived
description: Document written by `mise run video-derive` as `derived.json`.

reference_check.description: The comparison against the pinned frame capture, once it ran.

DerivedColumns.description: Per-frame columns, one entry per row of the capture's tick log, in its order.

palette_step.description: Whether a palette write took effect at the frame.

render_tick.description: Render-store tick the frame is paired with.

DerivedRules.description: The rule behind each derived column.

DerivedSource.description: The files this document was computed from, as SHA-256 in lower-case hex.

meta_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the `meta.json` beside this file.

video_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the `capture.avi` beside this file.

oneOf.description: True on the frame a palette write took effect (`palettes.changes[].frame`).

PixelEqual.description: Pixel-equal fractions of the compared pages: the best match each page found in the video.

ReferenceCheck.description:
The video compared against the pinned frame capture of the same film.

Each kept page's RGB (through its own palette) is searched in the video at
`emu_frame - capture_start_frame - 1` (the video frame of the log row at `emu_frame`) plus an offset within `search`, over the rows in `rows`.

band_pages.description: The remaining pages: some row matches no frame in the window.

capture_digest.description: The `references.toml` digest of the frame capture compared against.

exact_pages.description: Pages whose best match was pixel-equal everywhere.

offsets.description: Best offset, as a decimal string (`"-1"`), to the number of pages that found it first.

rows.description: First and last row compared, inclusive.

skipped.description: Pages whose search window left the video, so they were not compared.

split_pages.description:
Pages with no exact match whose every row equals that row of some video frame in the
window `-2..=+4` around the paired frame: a tear between two frames.

oneOf.description:
`slot_clock - slot_ticks + 1`, or `film_tick` where the ticks word exceeds the clock
(ADR 0057).
`film_tick`: the capture logged no slot words.
